item.title: CALL FOR PAPERS: BETWEEN ITALY AND THE BOSPHORUS. ROME AS CENTRE AND PERIPHERY IN THE BYZANTINE ‘OECUMENE’ (5TH-8TH CENTURIES)
item.description: SUBJECT After the 5th century’s discontinuing of the imperial office in the West, Rome was subjected to the short-lived rule of Odoacer, before coming under the more stable control of the Ostrogothic king Theodoric, invited by Constantinople’s court to occupy Italy in the emperor’s name. Under the Ostrogoths, Italy was consequently reorganized as an independent polity formally subordinate to the imperial government, thus preserving a distinctly Roman administrative structure.
